3 days in Lisbon itinerary: Alfama, Belém, Baixa | Day in Portugal
A 3-day Lisbon itinerary: Alfama and miradouros on day 1, Belém on day 2, Baixa and Chiado on day 3. What to book and what to skip.
3 days in Lisbon — Alfama, Belém, then the flat grid
Lisbon itinerary · 3 days
3 days in Lisbon: Alfama first, Belém second, the flat grid last.
A walking itinerary if you sleep in the centre. The tram is a ride through streets you can also walk. Sintra, Cascais and Évora are each their own day — not an extra on day 3.
Lisbon and the Tagus seen from Castelo de São Jorge toward Praça do Comércio
Day 1 — Alfama, one miradouro, and the tram only if a seat is empty
Start at the Sé and walk up to Largo das Portas do Sol and Miradouro de Santa Luzia. The view over the roofs is free.
Keep climbing to Miradouro da Senhora do Monte if you want the whole city in one glance. It is a hill, not a taxi problem, unless your knees say otherwise.

Tram 28E is a Carris tram from Martim Moniz to Campo de Ourique (Prazeres), through Graça, Santa Luzia, the Sé and Chiado. It does not go to Belém. The queue is at the first stop. Walk the same streets, or board further along when a seat is actually empty.
Route and stops:
Carris 28E
. São Jorge Castle is optional. Most of the postcard is the view from the miradouros outside the walls.

Sintra day trip from Lisbon: train, Pena, Regaleira | Day in Portugal
How to do Sintra in a day from Lisbon: the Rossio train, bus 434, a timed Pena Palace ticket, the Moorish Castle and Quinta da Regaleira.
Sintra day trip from Lisbon — train, then the palace clock
Sintra day trip
From Lisbon · Sintra
Sintra in a day: the train is easy, the palace clock is not.

Pena, the Moorish Castle and Quinta da Regaleira are three visits, not one stroll. The train from Rossio is the simple part. The part that ruins the day is a palace ticket timed for the door, with a hill still in front of you.
The National Palace of Pena above the trees in Sintra
What you are actually choosing
Park and National Palace of Pena.

The coloured palace is inside the park, up the hill. Parques de Sintra’s Essential Visit — park plus the palace interior — is €20 for ages 18–64, €18 for ages 6–17 and for over-65s, and €65 for a family of two adults and two youths. Checked 6 November 2026 on the
Pena page

. The park is listed 09:00–19:00, last admission 18:00. The palace is listed 09:30–18:30, last ticket 17:30 and last admission 18:00. A shuttle inside the park runs about every 15 minutes. Check before you go. Other tickets (park only, guided, a longer interior) are on the same page; the price that matters is the one next to the name you select.

The time on a palace ticket is the time at the palace door, not at the park gate. Parques de Sintra says to allow about 30 minutes between the two, on foot or on the shuttle, and that there is no tolerance if you are late. A missed slot is not refunded. Read that on
their ticket conditions
before you pick a slot.
Moorish Castle.

The walls above the town. Adult €12, youth and senior €10, family (two adults and two youths) €33. Open 09:30–18:00, last entry 17:30. The staffed ticket office closes from 12:00 to 13:00; the machines stay on. Same check,
the castle page
, 6 November 2026. Private cars are not allowed on the access road.
Stone walls of the Moorish Castle above Sintra
Photo: travelmag.com,
Quinta da Regaleira.

The palace and gardens on the edge of the historic centre, including the initiation well. From January 2026 the foundation’s tariff is €20 for ages 18–64, €15 for ages 6–17 and for over-65s, free under 5, and €60 for a family of two adults or seniors and two youths. In October–December the gate opens at 10:00, last entry is 17:30 and the garden closes at 18:30. April–September it opens at 09:00 and closes at 19:30. Slots are every half hour, with up to one hour of lateness. Closed 1 January and 24, 25 and 31 December. Checked 6 November 2026 on
regaleira.pt
. The foundation says the only authorised online till is
, and that it does not answer for tickets bought anywhere else.
Quinta da Regaleira in Sintra, the palace among the gardens
Photo: Diego Delso,
The train, then the bus — in that order

Urban trains run from Lisboa Rossio to Sintra. Parques de Sintra also lists Oriente and Entrecampos as departure stations. On CP’s urban timetable for Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays, the 06:01 from Rossio is timed into Sintra at 06:41 — 40 minutes. Other columns on the same sheet end at Mira Sintra-Meleças, short of Sintra. Read the destination on the board. The sheet is
CP’s Lisbon urban timetable
. Check it for your date. Tickets are bought at the station, not as a reserved seat.
From Sintra station, Parques de Sintra sends you to Pena and to the Moorish Castle on bus 434 (Scotturb). The operator’s own site,
Sintra 434

, says the 434 starts every day at 08:50, about every 10 minutes, and that the circuit serves Pena, the Moorish Castle and the National Palace in the centre. The same FAQ gives the last departure from Pena as 19:08 in one answer and 19:00 in the next, and says the service ends at 18:40. Use the page the morning you go. A day ticket for the 434 and the 435 is €13.50, with 8% off online, valid 24 hours from the first validation. It does not include palace or castle entry.
Regaleira is not on the 434. The operator puts it on the 435 (Monserrate circuit), which the same FAQ starts at 09:00. You can also walk over from the historic centre once you are down from the hill.
A day that fits the clock

Book the Pena palace slot late enough that the train, the 434 from 08:50, and the 30 minutes inside the park still land you at the door on time. A slot at 09:30 is how people miss the palace. Late morning is the one that survives a delay.

Do the castle on the way down if the 434 stops there and you still have legs. Leave Regaleira for the afternoon: in November last entry is 17:30, and the official till is the one to use. Two of the three is a good day. All three is a march, and only if Pena was the morning and Regaleira is the last slot you can still make.
Buy Pena on the Parques de Sintra till first. If you would rather compare a reseller’s calendar:
Pena Palace and park on Tiqets
Castle, if you want it in the same basket:
Moorish Castle tickets
For Regaleira, start at
the foundation’s till
. A reseller page exists —
Quinta da Regaleira on Tiqets
— and the foundation has said it will not sort out tickets bought off its own site. Read that before you pay anyone else.
Guided days from Lisbon, if nobody wants the timetable:
Sintra day trips on Tiqets
A hire car does not solve Sintra

Parques de Sintra says private vehicles are not allowed up to Pena or to the Moorish Castle. You park in the historic centre or in the peripheral car parks and still take the bus or a trail. A car earns its place only if the same day continues to the coast. Pick it up when you leave Lisbon, not for the cobbles:
local rental firms in Lisbon on Localrent
Can you do Pena, the castle and Regaleira in one day?

The train is about 40 minutes. The palace time is at the door, and the park asks for about 30 minutes before that. The 434 does not start until 08:50. Two of the three is comfortable. All three only works with a late-morning Pena slot and Regaleira at the end, and it will feel like a march.
Do you have to book Pena ahead?
Yes. The palace ticket is a date and a time. Parques de Sintra says there is no delay tolerance, you cannot go in early, and a missed slot is not refunded.
Does the 434 ticket include the monuments?
No. Sintra 434 says the day ticket is the bus. Palace, castle and Regaleira are separate tickets.

Cascais day trip from Lisbon: train, bay, Boca do Inferno | Day in Portugal
Cascais in a day from Lisbon: the Cais do Sodré train, the bay, Carcavelos, and the walk to Boca do Inferno. Not the same day as Sintra.
Cascais day trip — one train along the water
Cascais day trip
From Lisbon · the Cascais line
Cascais in a day: one train, the bay, and the hole in the cliff.
This is the easy day. The same urban train that stops at Belém keeps going along the river and then the sea. Do not bolt Sintra onto it. The hills and the coast are two mornings, not one.
The bay at Cascais, with the town along the water
Photo: Herbert wie,
Cais do Sodré, then stay on the train

Cascais trains leave from Cais do Sodré, on the green metro line. CP’s urban timetable, in the Monday-to-Friday block, times the 05:30 from Cais do Sodré into Cascais at 06:10 — 40 minutes on the train that stops everywhere. Through the middle of the day the sheet shows a departure about every 20 minutes (10:40, 11:00, 11:20, and so on), with a tighter pattern in the weekday peaks and a faster semi-fast that skips some stops. Belém is on the way: the 10:40 from Cais do Sodré is timed at Belém at 10:48. The sheet is
CP’s Cascais-line timetable
. It has carried notes about replacement buses when the line is being worked on. Check the day, on
cp.pt
, before you treat 40 minutes as a promise.
Sit on the left going out if you want the water. Tickets are from the machines at Cais do Sodré. This is an urban train: no reserved seat, and no need to book one.
What to do when you get off
The bay.
Cascais station is the end of the line, in the town, by the water. The bay in front of the centre is the swim if the weather is kind and you do not need a wave. It is a town beach, not a secret one.
Carcavelos
is an earlier stop on the same timetable, before Estoril and Monte Estoril. Get off there if the point of the day is a long beach. Stay on to Cascais if the point is the town.
Boca do Inferno

is the cliff and the blowhole west of the centre. It is a walk along the coast from town, not a second train. On a calm day it is a viewing platform. On a rough day it is the reason the name exists. There is no ticket.
The sea cliffs at Boca do Inferno, Cascais
Photo: Jakub Hałun,

Guincho, the open Atlantic beach further west, is not a stop on this train. If that is the swim you want, it is a bus or a car from Cascais, and it is a different hour of the day. Do not promise it to yourself and also promise Boca do Inferno and a late lunch back in Lisbon.
What to skip
Sintra the same day.
The 434 up to Pena does not start from Cascais station. See
the Sintra day
on its own morning.
A hire car for this line.
The train is the point. A car helps if you are going on to Guincho or to a villa off the stations:
compare local cars in Lisbon
Belém on the way back only if you still have a slot.
The stop is there —
day 2 of the Lisbon itinerary
— but a cloister ticket you have already missed is just a façade from the platform.
How long is the train from Lisbon to Cascais?
About 40 minutes on the stopping train. CP’s timetable times 05:30 from Cais do Sodré to 06:10 at Cascais. Faster weekday trains skip some stops. Check cp.pt, including any replacement bus.
Where do you swim?
The bay at Cascais, in town. For a long beach, leave the train at Carcavelos. Guincho is further west and not on the train.
Can you combine Cascais and Sintra?
Not if you want either of them. One is a train along the water. The other is a timed palace door and a bus that starts at 08:50 from Sintra station.
